source: loops/loop-025/research-appeal-patterns.md — patterns abstracted from public Japanese job-media ads (バイトル/タウンワーク/マイナビバイト/リクナビ派遣ほか, read 2026-11-04). No ad text is copied; only the structures are recorded.

patterns.name: headline-is-the-job
patterns.rule: The headline is the job itself, with the deciding conditions attached; never a greeting and never conditions alone.

patterns.name: short-assertions
patterns.rule: Appeals are short assertions, one point per sentence. No long explanatory prose; a sentence says one thing.

patterns.name: condition-with-meaning
patterns.rule: State each condition together with what it means in the reader's life (from the audience), in the same breath. Never end at a restatement of the condition.

patterns.name: barrier-with-ground
patterns.rule: A low-barrier appeal (no experience needed, etc.) is paired with the concrete ground the materials give — the work's concrete tasks. Never invent support systems, training, or staff that the materials do not state.

patterns.name: numbers-early-and-exact
patterns.rule: The concrete numbers (wage, hours, caps) stay in the sentences that carry them, exactly as stated; do not bury, round, or convert them.

patterns.name: no-boilerplate-closings
patterns.rule: Never close an appeal sentence with a boilerplate request (ご確認ください / ご検討ください / お問い合わせください). End assertions plainly. An inquiry invitation may appear only on a sentence that states an item is not stated (未記載), at most once in the copy.

patterns.name: cta-at-the-end-only
patterns.rule: Application and inquiry calls live at the page's closing, not inside appeal sentences.
